1H (Number Theory)

Words: 144 Articles: 1
Paper 1 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 144
1H OurBigBook.com
An integral positive definite binary quadratic form
[a,b,c](x,y)=ax2+bxy+cy2
(1)
is reduced when
∣b∣≤a≤c,
(2)
with b≥0 when ∣b∣=a or a=c. Its discriminant is D=b2−4ac.
For D=−20, reduction gives 3a2≤20, so a=1 or 2. Since b2≡D(mod4), b is even. If a=1, then ∣b∣≤1 forces b=0, and c=5. If a=2, then b∈{−2,0,2}; integrality of
c=8b2+20​
(3)
leaves b=±2 and c=3, and the boundary convention retains only b=2. Hence the complete list is
[1,0,5]and[2,2,3]​.
(4)
Now suppose the prime p=5 is represented by x2+5y2. If p=2, the equation is impossible modulo four, so p is odd. The integers x and y then have opposite parity, and therefore
p=x2+5y2≡1(mod4).
(5)
Also x≡0(mod5), since otherwise 5∣p; hence
p≡x2≡1 or 4(mod5).
(6)
The Chinese remainder theorem gives the stronger conclusion
p≡1 or 9(mod20).
(7)
In particular,
p≡1,3,7, or 9(mod20)​,
(8)
as required.

a OurBigBook.com
In Shannon-Fano coding, a symbol of probability pi​ is assigned length
ℓi​=⌈−log2​pi​⌉,
(19)
and codewords of those lengths are chosen in lexicographic probability intervals; the Kraft inequality guarantees that a binary prefix code exists. Huffman coding repeatedly merges the two least probable current symbols, builds a binary tree from the resulting merges, and labels its two branches by zero and one. Reading from the root to each leaf gives an optimal prefix code.

4F (Automata and Formal Languages)

Words: 142 Articles: 1
Paper 1 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 142
4F OurBigBook.com
An alphabet Σ is a finite nonempty set of symbols. A word over an alphabet is a finite sequence of symbols from Σ, including the empty word ϵ; the set of all words is Σ∗. A formal language over Σ is any subset L⊆Σ∗.
A regular expression is defined recursively from ∅, ϵ, and the individual symbols a∈Σ by the operations of finite union, concatenation, and Kleene star. Its language is defined by
L(∅)=∅,L(ϵ)={ϵ},L(a)={a},
(29)
L(R∣S)=L(R)∪L(S),L(RS)=L(R)L(S),L(R∗)=L(R)∗.
(30)
There are only countably many regular expressions: each is a finite word over a finite collection of symbols and punctuation. On the other hand, for every nonempty finite alphabet, Σ∗ is countably infinite, so its power set P(Σ∗) is uncountable by the Cantor theorem. Thus there are uncountably many languages but only countably many languages denoted by regular expressions. Consequently
some languages over Σ are not regular​.
(31)

At a current value β, put

(37)
and define the working response
zi​=ηi​+(Yi​−μi​)g′(μi​).

I(β)=XTWX,
(39)

Indeed, the jth component of the latter is
∑i=1n​ai​σ2V(μi​)g′(μi​)Xij​(Yi​−μi​)​,

Substitution into the Fisher-scoring update gives
βnew=β+(XTWX)−1XTW(z−Xβ)=(XTWX)−1XTWz.
(42)
By part (b), this is the weighted least squares fit of the working response z on X. Both z and W are recomputed from the current fitted means after every update. Fisher scoring for a generalized linear model is therefore the iteratively reweighted least squares algorithm.

Let each mass be m and each spring constant be k, with the xi​ denoting longitudinal displacements from equilibrium. The Lagrangian is
L=2m​∑i=14​x˙i2​−2k​[(x2​−x1​)2+(x3​−x2​)2+(x4​−x3​)2].
(60)
The inverse coordinate transformation is
x1​=q1​+q3​,x4​=q1​−q3​,x2​=q2​+q4​,x3​=q2​−q4​.
(61)
Substitution gives
L=m(q˙​12​+q˙​22​+q˙​32​+q˙​42​)−k[(q2​−q1​)2+(q4​−q3​)2+2q42​]​.
(62)
Thus the Euler-Lagrange equations separate into a symmetric pair,
mq¨​1​+k(q1​−q2​)=0,mq¨​2​+k(q2​−q1​)=0,
(63)
and an antisymmetric pair,
mq¨​3​+k(q3​−q4​)=0,mq¨​4​+k(3q4​−q3​)=0.
(64)
The symmetric normal modes are:
  • q1​=q2​, corresponding to (x1​,x2​,x3​,x4​)∝(1,1,1,1) and the translational frequency
ω0​=0​;
(65)
  • q1​=−q2​, corresponding to (1,−1,−1,1) and
ωs​=m2k​​​.
(66)
For antisymmetric modes, the squared dimensionless frequencies are the eigenvalues of
(1−1​−13​),
(67)
namely 2∓2​. They give
ω−​=mk​(2−2​)​​,(q3​,q4​)∝(1,2​−1),
(68)
and
ω+​=mk​(2+2​)​​,(q3​,q4​)∝(1,−1−2​).

In the original coordinates their mode shapes are respectively
(1,2​−1,1−2​,−1)
(70)
and
(1,−1−2​,1+2​,−1).

9D (Cosmology)

Words: 156 Articles: 1
Paper 1 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 156
9D OurBigBook.com
The Hubble parameter is the fractional expansion rate
H=aa˙​.
(72)
Here ρ is the homogeneous energy density, k∈{−1,0,1} records the sign of the spatial curvature of an FLRW universe, and R is the fixed curvature length scale used with the dimensionless scale factor a(t).
Energy-momentum conservation in a homogeneous expanding universe gives the continuity equation
ρ˙​+3H(ρ+P)=0.
(73)
Differentiate the Friedmann equation
H2=3c28πG​(ρ−R2a2kc2​).
(74)
Using a˙/a=H and the continuity equation gives
H˙=−c24πG​(ρ+P)+3c28πG​R2a2kc2​.
(75)
Eliminating the curvature term with the Friedmann equation yields
H˙+H2=−3c24πG​(ρ+3P).
(76)
Since H˙+H2=a¨/a, this is the Raychaudhuri equation
aa¨​=−3c24πG​(ρ+3P)​.
(77)
Under the strong energy condition ρ+3P≥0, one has a¨≤0. Thus a(t) is concave, and for t<t0​ it lies below its tangent at the present time:
a(t)≤a(t0​)+a˙(t0​)(t−t0​)=a(t0​)[1−H0​(t0​−t)].
(78)
The right side vanishes at t=t0​−H0−1​. A positive scale factor therefore cannot extend regularly to that time; it must reach the Big Bang singularity at some tBB​≥t0​−H0−1​. Equivalently,
t0​−tBB​≤H0−1​​.
(79)

a

Solution

a OurBigBook.com
A register machine has finitely many natural-number registers, a finite set of labelled states, and instructions that increment a register, conditionally decrement and branch according to whether a register is zero, or halt. A program is a finite sequence of such labelled instructions, and a configuration records the current instruction together with every current register value.
Given k inputs, place them in designated input registers and initialize the remaining registers to zero. The machine computes a partial computable function f:Nk⇀N when it halts with output f(x) in the output register exactly for x∈domf and runs forever otherwise.
To encode a machine, encode every instruction by a natural number using effective encodings of its opcode, register number, and target labels. Encode the resulting finite sequence by a Gödel numbering, for example through iterated pairing or prime powers. Effective decoding gives an enumeration (Pn​) of machine programs, so the unary function computed by program code n may be denoted fn,1​.

b

Words: 105 Articles: 1

Solution

Words: 105
b OurBigBook.com
The partial recursive functions form the smallest class containing the zero function, successor function, and projection functions and closed under composition, primitive recursion, and unbounded minimization.
Fix a register machine P with k inputs. By the permitted result, its complete configuration after t steps,
S(x,t),
(106)
is a recursive function of the inputs and time. The predicate H(x,t) saying that this configuration is halted is therefore recursive. Its halting time is the partial recursive function
τ(x)=μt[H(x,t)],
(107)
where unbounded minimization is undefined when no halting time exists. Extracting the output register from a configuration is recursive, so
f(x)=out(S(x,τ(x)))
(108)
is partial recursive. Hence every partial computable function is partial recursive.

g(e)=fe,1​(e)+1=g(e)+1,
(109)
which is impossible. This is the usual diagonal argument behind the noncomputability of the diagonal halting set.

The function h is also not partial computable. On every odd input it is defined, and
h(n)=0⟺fn,1​(n) is undefined(n odd),
(110)
because the value in the halting case is fn,1​(n)+1≥1. Thus a machine computing h would decide diagonal halting for odd program indices simply by running h(n) and testing whether its output is zero.
That restricted problem remains undecidable. By the padding lemma, an arbitrary machine can effectively be replaced by an equivalent machine having an odd code—for example by adding unreachable instructions until the chosen effective encoding has the required parity. This gives a computable reduction from unrestricted diagonal halting to diagonal halting on odd indices. A decider obtained from h would therefore decide the full diagonal halting problem, a contradiction. Hence
h is not partial computable​.
(111)

Kilometres is an ordinal categorical variable: its five levels have a meaningful order. Treating it as an ordinary factor would use four indicator variables and hence four unrelated regression coefficients. Converting the levels to numerical scores instead imposes a single linear trend across successive mileage bands. This is more parsimonious and gives greater precision when that trend is a reasonable approximation, although it also assumes that adjacent levels are equally spaced in their effect.

log(Paymentperpolicyyr)

Maschke's theorem says that if H is a finite group and the characteristic of a field F does not divide ∣H∣, then every finite-dimensional F-representation of H is semisimple.
To prove it, let W be an invariant subspace of a representation V, and choose any linear projection P:V→W. Average its conjugates:
P=∣H∣1​∑h∈H​ρ(h)Pρ(h)−1.
(176)
The scalar ∣H∣−1 exists by the characteristic assumption. Reindexing the sum shows that P commutes with every ρ(g). Since each summand restricts to the identity on W, so does P; hence P is an equivariant projection onto W. Its kernel is an invariant complement, and induction on dimV decomposes V into irreducible representations.
The isometry group of Z is the infinite dihedral group
G=⟨t,s∣s2=1, sts=t−1⟩.
(177)
Let ρ be a nonfaithful finite-dimensional complex representation. Its nontrivial normal kernel contains tm for some m>0, by the stated hint, so ρ factors through the finite quotient
⟨t,s∣tm=s2=1, sts=t−1⟩.
(178)
Maschke's theorem decomposes this quotient representation into irreducibles. To bound their dimensions, choose a t-eigenvector v with eigenvalue λ in an irreducible constituent. The relation gives
t(sv)=st−1v=λ−1sv,
(179)
so span{v,sv} is invariant under both generators. Irreducibility makes it the whole constituent, whose dimension is therefore at most two. This proves the result on nonfaithful representations of the infinite dihedral group.
For the requested representation of (Z,+), let its generator act on the polynomials of degree at most one by translation:
(Tp)(x)=p(x+1).
(180)
In the basis (1,x),
T=(10​11​).
(181)
This is a nontrivial Jordan block, so it is not diagonalizable. A direct sum of one-dimensional subrepresentations would make T diagonalizable, proving that this nonsemisimple translation representation of the infinite cyclic group has the required property.
Finally, on V=C[x]≤2​ define
(Tp)(x)=p(x+1),(Sp)(x)=p(−x).
(182)
Then S2=I and STS=T−1, so these operators define a quadratic-polynomial representation of the infinite dihedral group. In the basis (1,x,x2) they are
T=​100​110​121​​,S=​100​0−10​001​​.
(183)
Here (T−I)2=0 but (T−I)3=0, so T consists of one size-three Jordan block. If V were a direct sum of subrepresentations of dimensions at most two, then T would be block diagonal with Jordan blocks of sizes at most two, a contradiction. Thus this representation has the required failure of decomposition.

The equilibrium points of a dynamical system form the three branch families
x=0,qquadx=±2μ​(μ≥0),qquadx=±μ−a​(μ≥a).
(351)
For a simple equilibrium, fixed point stability for an autonomous differential equation is determined by the sign of fx​. On the three families,
branchx=0x2=2μx2=μ−a​fx​−2μ(μ−a)−4μ(μ+a)2(μ−a)(μ+a).​​

Thus solid branches in the figure are stable and dashed branches are unstable.
If a<0, the pair x=±μ−a​ emerges stably from x=0 at μ=a in a pitchfork bifurcation. At μ=0, the pair x=±2μ​ meets x=0 with unstable nonzero branches; after reversing the parameter orientation this is a subcritical pitchfork bifurcation. At μ=−a, the two positive branches cross and exchange stability, as do the two negative branches, giving two simultaneous transcritical bifurcations at x=±−2a​.
If a=0, every branch meets at (μ,x)=(0,0). For μ<0 only the stable trivial branch exists. For μ>0, x=0 is stable, the inner branches x=±μ​ are unstable, and the outer branches x=±2μ​ are stable. This is a degenerate fifth-order bifurcation rather than a generic pitchfork.
If a>0, a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation occurs at μ=0: the trivial branch loses stability and the stable branches x=±2μ​ emerge. At μ=a, the unstable branches x=±μ−a​ meet the trivial branch, which regains stability; this is the parameter-reversed form of a subcritical pitchfork bifurcation.
These cases comprise the bifurcations of the 2020 Cambridge quintic system.

so its survival probability decays as e−Γt/ℏ and its lifetime is
τ=Γℏ​=2ℏπ3mU02​a4​.​

Let two systems exchange energy inside an otherwise isolated composite system, so E1​+E2​=E is fixed. By the Second law of thermodynamics, equilibrium maximizes the total entropy
Stot​(E1​)=S1​(E1​)+S2​(E−E1​).
(407)
At an interior maximum,
0=dE1​dStot​​=∂E1​∂S1​​−∂E2​∂S2​​=T1​1​−T2​1​.
(408)
Thus T1​=T2​, which is entropy maximization under thermal contact and the condition for thermal equilibrium.
Stability requires this entropy maximum to be locally strict, so each ordinary subsystem has a concave entropy-energy relation. Since
∂E2∂2S​=∂E∂​(T1​)=−T21​∂E∂T​<0,
(409)
one has ∂T/∂E>0, or equivalently
∂T∂E​>0.​
(410)
This is the entropy concavity and positive heat capacity criterion.
Now let N↑​=αN and N↓​=(1−α)N. Because the spins are distinguishable, the number of microstates is the binomial coefficient
Ω=(αNN​)=(αN)!((1−α)N)!N!​.
(411)
The Boltzmann entropy S=kB​logΩ and the Stirling formula give, to leading order for large N,
S(α)=−NkB​[αlogα+(1−α)log(1−α)].​
(412)
The total energy is
E(α)=N(αϵ−(1−α)ϵ)=Nϵ(2α−1).​
(413)
Therefore
T1​=dE/dαdS/dα​=2ϵkB​​log(α1−α​).
(414)
Solving for the up-spin fraction gives the independent spin-one-half two-level system result
α(T)=1+e2ϵ/(kB​T)1​.​
(415)
For ordinary positive absolute temperature,
0≤α<21​,​
(416)
with α→0 as T→0+ and α→1/2 as T→+∞. Since the spectrum is bounded above, the population-inverted range 1/2<α≤1 is also mathematically possible and corresponds to negative temperature; α=1/2 is the infinite-temperature state.
Substitution gives
E(T)=−Nϵtanh(kB​Tϵ​),
(417)
and direct differentiation yields
dTdE​=kB​T2Nϵ2​sech2(kB​Tϵ​)>0.​
(418)
Thus the energy increases with temperature throughout either finite-temperature branch, in particular throughout the required positive-temperature range.

a OurBigBook.com
For a fixed shift s that is not an eigenvalue, inverse iteration is the power method applied to (A−sI)−1. Before normalization, the kth vector is proportional to
(A−sI)−kx(0)=∑i=1n​ci​(λi​−s)−kwi​.
(497)
If s<λ1​, factor out the first coefficient:
(A−sI)−kx(0)=c1​(λ1​−s)−k[w1​+∑i=2n​c1​ci​​(λi​−sλ1​−s​)kwi​].
(498)
Every ratio in parentheses lies strictly between zero and one. The bracket therefore tends to w1​, and normalization in the Euclidean norm gives
x(k)⟶sgn(c1​)w1​.​
(499)
This proves the stated convergence to w1​ or −w1​ and exhibits the convergence of fixed-shift inverse iteration rate.
Now suppose λm​<s<λm+1​. The closest eigenvalue to s is one of λm​ and λm+1​.
  • If s−λm​<λm+1​−s, the direction approaches wm​, but (λm​−s)−1<0, so consecutive iterates alternate signs.
  • If s−λm​>λm+1​−s, the iterates approach one fixed sign of wm+1​ because (λm+1​−s)−1>0.
  • At the midpoint, the two dominant inverse eigenvalues have equal modulus and opposite signs. Generic iterates alternate between the two normalized combinations proportional to cm​wm​+cm+1​wm+1​ and −cm​wm​+cm+1​wm+1​.
Finally, if λn​<s, the closest eigenvalue is λn​ and its inverse eigenvalue is negative. Thus the direction approaches the line spanned by wn​, while normalized vectors alternate between the two signs. These cases are the sign behavior of fixed-shift inverse iteration.

Expanding the denominator gives
sk​=λ1​+ϵ2∑i≥2​ai2​(λi​−λ1​)+O(ϵ4).
(502)
The question prints this as sk​=λ1​−Kϵ2+O(ϵ4), so its sign convention requires
K=i≥2∑​ai2​(λ1​−λi​)<0​

unless every ai​ vanishes. Equivalently, −K is the positive quadratic Rayleigh-quotient error.
The shifted inverse solve has the spectral decomposition
y=c−1[λ1​−sk​1​w1​+ϵ∑i≥2​λi​−sk​ai​​wi​].
(504)
Only relative coefficients matter after normalization, so factor out (λ1​−sk​)−1:
y∥w1​+ϵ∑i≥2​ai​λi​−sk​λ1​−sk​​wi​.
(505)
From the shift expansion,
λ1​−sk​=Kϵ2+O(ϵ4),
(506)
whereas, for i≥2,
λi​−sk​=(λi​−λ1​)+Kϵ2+O(ϵ4).
(507)
Consequently
ϵai​λi​−sk​λ1​−sk​​=ϵ3λi​−λ1​Kai​​+O(ϵ5).

x(k+1)=c1−1​(w1​+ϵ3i≥2∑​bi​wi​+O(ϵ5)),bi​=λi​−λ1​Kai​​.​

Thus an O(ϵ) eigenvector-direction error becomes O(ϵ3) in one step, proving the Local cubic convergence of Rayleigh quotient iteration for this symmetric matrix.
